title: August was the joint hottest month on record | New Scientist
description: Global warming and a record El Niño have pushed Earth’s temperature more than 1.5°C above the pre-industrial average, and further heat is on the way
author: Alec Luhn

title: Earliest evidence of habitual drug use found in teeth in Indonesia | New Scientist
description: Strange, rounded grooves in prehistoric teeth are thought to have been made by regularly sucking whole betel nuts to extract a pain-relieving compound. This marks the earliest known example of probable substance addiction
author: Alice Klein

title: Heat spikes over Tibet may help explain severe Californian flooding | New Scientist
description: Unusually high temperatures over the mountainous region can kick-start a chain of events that ultimately leads to a severe deluge on the US West Coast, scientists say
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Bursts of ‘pink noise’ during sleep seem to help clear waste from brain | New Scientist
description: The human brain flushes out waste products while we sleep and now it seems that certain sounds might enhance the process
author: Carissa Wong

title: Terence Tao: AI companies are harming mathematics | New Scientist
description: AI firms are making new mathematical discoveries at a rapid pace, but not sticking around to help unpick the new proofs. That is not the way to advance our understanding, says mathematician Terence Tao
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: NASA’s next major telescope might see alien oceans and rainbows | New Scientist
description: The upcoming Habitable Worlds Observatory should be able to spot the glint of water on habitable planets, and maybe more
author: Jonathan O’Callaghan
